column1: # The package set, and the single source of truth for it.
# build/BuildNugets.sh packs in this order, the CI workflows generate their package tables from it,
# and tests/OpenTok.Net.iOS.PackageTests reads it. Adding a package means adding a row here and a
# project under src/ — nothing else keeps a second copy of the list.
# Both rows are binding projects and both carry native payload, but they are not the same shape:
#   * OpenTok.Net.iOS binds OpenTok.xcframework, a *static* archive, embedded into the binding
#     assembly's own native companion. It has a real ApiDefinition.cs.
#   * OpenTok.Net.Transformers.iOS carries OpenTokTransformers.xcframework, a *dynamic* framework,
#     travelling beside the assembly as <Assembly>.resources.zip. It has no managed API at all —
#     the classes that use it (OTVideoTransformer, OTAudioTransformer) are already in the binding
#     above, and the core SDK dlopens the framework when one of them is constructed. See
#     src/OpenTok.Transformers.md.
# The two are independent: the transformers package does not depend on the binding, and the binding
# does not depend on it. A consumer adds the transformers package only if it wants background blur,
# background replacement or noise suppression, and pays ~68 MB for the privilege.
# Columns
#   id       the NuGet package id, which is also the directory under src/ and the .csproj basename
#   kind     binding - has a real ApiDefinition.cs and a managed API
#            payload - native payload only, empty ApiDefinition.cs, no managed API
#   deps     other ids in this repository it depends on, comma separated, or -
# id
OpenTok.Net.iOS
OpenTok.Net.Transformers.iOS
